problem.title: Existence of an odd perfect number below a fixed bound
problem.informal_statement:
Decide whether some odd integer n with 1 < n < 10^2200 satisfies sigma(n) = 2n, where sigma is the sum-of-divisors function.

The bound is stated explicitly so the search region is finite; no claim is made that the region is small enough to enumerate.

target_claim.statement: There exists an odd integer n with 1 < n < 10^2200 such that sigma(n) = 2n.

assumption_claims.statement: An integer n >= 1 is perfect iff sigma(n) = 2n, where sigma(n) is the sum of all positive divisors of n.
For coprime positive integers a and b, sigma(a*b) = sigma(a)*sigma(b).
Every odd perfect number has the form p^e * m^2 with p an odd prime, p congruent to e congruent to 1 modulo 4, and gcd(p, m) = 1.

formalization.statement: exists n : N, Odd(n) and 1 < n and n < 10^2200 and sigma(n) = 2*n
quantifiers: exists n in N with 1 < n < 10^2200

quantifier_mapping: odd integer n strictly between 1 and 10^2200
definition_mapping: sum of all positive divisors of n, including n
assumption_delta: The informal statement says 'below a fixed bound'; the formalization pins that bound to 10^2200 and no other value.
edge_case_delta: n = 1 is excluded explicitly because sigma(1) = 1, not 2.

success_criteria: an exhibited odd n with a checked sigma(n) = 2n
or a refutation covering the whole stated region
stopping_rules: stop when the stated region is fully covered by checked exclusions
stop when no obligation has been discharged for two consecutive review points
